fn.en: Talk about your plans and arrangements for the near future.

items.q: To take a file from the internet onto your phone: to ___ it.
To put your name and password in: to ___ on.
To send somebody a message so you are in contact: to get in ___.
To send a photo to other people: to ___ it.
To turn the phone completely off: to ___ it off.
A difficult thing you decide to try for thirty days: a ___.

sub.en: Look at the pairs. Which one is a decision, and which one is already in the diary?

items.q: I ___ walk ten thousand steps a day. (I decided last week)
items.why: going to = an intention or a decision. Present Continuous = an arrangement already fixed with somebody else.

items.q: I ___ a friend from university on Friday. (we agreed it last week)
How ___ you going to do it?
I ___ look at my phone before breakfast.
___ you doing anything on Friday night?
We ___ take the stairs instead of the lift.
The train ___ at ten past six. (the timetable says so)
items.why: A timetable takes the Present Simple, not a future form.

items.q: I ___ it really hard. (my prediction, based on how I feel)

rows: I’m meeting a friend on Friday.
She’s going to take up running.
___|We aren’t going to buy a car.
How are you going to do it?

use: I think I’m going to find it hard.
tts: Today I’m going to spend twenty-four hours without the internet. Usually, before I go to bed, I check Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, my email, and the weather and my calendar for the next day. I never completely switch off and stop thinking about work.
When I get up, I always look at my phone, and then go online and read the news. Most of my social life is online too, so I think I’m going to find it really hard.
Social media is very important for my job. Usually, I take photos of what I’m doing and share them. Tomorrow I’m not going to take any photos at all.

items.s: She is going to spend a whole day offline.
She usually checks her phone before bed.
She thinks it will be easy.
Social media matters for her job.
She is going to take photos and share them tomorrow.

tts: I think this thirty-day challenge idea is great. I’m definitely going to try it. — Me too. So, what are you going to do first?
I’m going to walk ten thousand steps a day. — Good idea. So, how are you going to do it?
Well, when I go out to the shops, I’m going to walk, not drive. I’m going to take the stairs instead of the lift and, twice a week, I’m going to walk to work, not get the bus.
Are you going to get one of those little things which count your steps?

acts.title: The week we switched everything off
text: We are going to spend next week without the internet, all four of us, and we have spent two evenings arguing about the rules.

The children are not going to use the tablet at all. That was the easy part; they agreed in about four seconds, which worries me. My husband is going to keep his work email, because he cannot switch that off and stay employed. I am going to keep nothing.

The arrangements are already a problem. I’m meeting a colleague on Wednesday and I don’t know where, because we always agree the place by message on the day. My daughter is playing in a concert on Thursday and the tickets are in an app.
We are not going to tell anybody we are doing it. If we tell people, it becomes a project, and then it becomes a thing we did instead of a thing we are doing.

items.s: The whole family is going offline for a week.
The husband is going to keep his work email.
She is meeting a colleague on Wednesday.
They are going to tell everybody about it.

The train is going to leave at ten past six.
The train is leaving at ten past six, the timetable says.

write.q: Write about your next week: 6 sentences. Two intentions with going to, two arrangements with the Present Continuous, one negative intention, and one timetable fact with the Present Simple.
write.model: Next week I’m going to walk to work every day instead of taking the bus. I’m also going to finish the report I have been avoiding since March. I’m meeting my sister on Tuesday evening and I’m seeing the dentist on Thursday at four, which I am less pleased about. I’m not going to look at my phone before breakfast. The train I take leaves at ten past seven, so this will all start earlier than I would like.

speak.q: Answer out loud: What are you going to do next week? What are you doing on Friday? What aren’t you going to do?
speak.model: Next week I’m going to walk to work every day. On Friday I’m meeting my sister for dinner — we agreed it last week. I’m not going to check my email at the weekend.
